solution: The order of a surd is the index of its root sign. In \(\sqrt[3]{7}\) the index is 3. Order = 3.
In \(5\sqrt{12}\) the root sign is a square root, so its index is 2 (the multiplier 5 does not affect the order). Order = 2.
In \(\sqrt[4]{10}\) the index of the root sign is 4. Order = 4.
\(\sqrt{39}\) is a square root, so the index of the root sign is 2. Order = 2.
In \(\sqrt[3]{18}\) the index of the root sign is 3. Order = 3.
51 is a rational number that is not a perfect cube, since \(3^3 = 27\) and \(4^3 = 64\). So \(\sqrt[3]{51}\) is irrational. Yes, \(\sqrt[3]{51}\) is a surd.
\(16 = 2^4\), so \(\sqrt[4]{16} = \sqrt[4]{2^4} = 2\), which is a rational number. No, \(\sqrt[4]{16}\) is not a surd.
81 is not a perfect fifth power, since \(2^5 = 32\) and \(3^5 = 243\). So \(\sqrt[5]{81}\) is irrational. Yes, \(\sqrt[5]{81}\) is a surd.
\(256 = 16^2\), so \(\sqrt{256} = 16\), which is a rational number. No, \(\sqrt{256}\) is not a surd.
\(64 = 4^3\), so \(\sqrt[3]{64} = 4\), which is a rational number. No, \(\sqrt[3]{64}\) is not a surd.
\(\frac{22}{7}\) is a positive rational number, but it is not the square of any rational number, so \(\sqrt{\frac{22}{7}}\) is irrational. Yes, \(\sqrt{\frac{22}{7}}\) is a surd.
\(\sqrt{52} = \sqrt{4 \times 13} = 2\sqrt{13}\). So the two surds are \(2\sqrt{13}\) and \(5\sqrt{13}\), which have the same order and the same radicand 13. They are like surds.
\(\sqrt{68} = \sqrt{4 \times 17} = 2\sqrt{17}\). So the two surds are \(2\sqrt{17}\) and \(5\sqrt{3}\); the radicands 17 and 3 are different. They are unlike surds.
\(4\sqrt{18} = 4\sqrt{9 \times 2} = 4 \times 3\sqrt{2} = 12\sqrt{2}\). So the two surds are \(12\sqrt{2}\) and \(7\sqrt{2}\), with the same radicand 2. They are like surds.
\(19\sqrt{12} = 19\sqrt{4 \times 3} = 19 \times 2\sqrt{3} = 38\sqrt{3}\). So the two surds are \(38\sqrt{3}\) and \(6\sqrt{3}\), with the same radicand 3. They are like surds.
Neither 22 nor 33 has a square factor, so \(5\sqrt{22}\) and \(7\sqrt{33}\) are already in simplest form and their radicands 22 and 33 are different. They are unlike surds.
\(\sqrt{75} = \sqrt{25 \times 3} = 5\sqrt{3}\). So the two surds are \(5\sqrt{5}\) and \(5\sqrt{3}\); the radicands 5 and 3 are different. They are unlike surds.
Take out the largest square factor: \(27 = 9 \times 3\). So \(\sqrt{27} = \sqrt{9 \times 3} = \sqrt{9} \times \sqrt{3} = 3\sqrt{3}\).
\(50 = 25 \times 2\), so \(\sqrt{50} = \sqrt{25} \times \sqrt{2} = 5\sqrt{2}\).
\(112 = 16 \times 7\), so \(\sqrt{112} = \sqrt{16} \times \sqrt{7} = 4\sqrt{7}\).
\(168 = 4 \times 42\), and 42 has no square factor. So \(\sqrt{168} = \sqrt{4} \times \sqrt{42} = 2\sqrt{42}\).

Write both as single square roots: \(7\sqrt{2} = \sqrt{49 \times 2} = \sqrt{98}\) and \(5\sqrt{3} = \sqrt{25 \times 3} = \sqrt{75}\). Since \(98 > 75\), we get \(\sqrt{98} > \sqrt{75}\). Therefore \(7\sqrt{2} > 5\sqrt{3}\).
Both are square roots already, so compare the radicands: \(247 < 274\). Therefore \(\sqrt{247} < \sqrt{274}\).
\(2\sqrt{7} = \sqrt{4 \times 7} = \sqrt{28}\), and the second surd is \(\sqrt{28}\). The radicands are equal. Therefore \(2\sqrt{7} = \sqrt{28}\).

solution: Write both as single square roots: \(4\sqrt{42} = \sqrt{16 \times 42} = \sqrt{672}\) and \(9\sqrt{2} = \sqrt{81 \times 2} = \sqrt{162}\). Since \(672 > 162\), we get \(\sqrt{672} > \sqrt{162}\). Therefore \(4\sqrt{42} > 9\sqrt{2}\).
Write both as single square roots: \(5\sqrt{3} = \sqrt{25 \times 3} = \sqrt{75}\) and \(9 = \sqrt{81}\). Since \(75 < 81\), we get \(\sqrt{75} < \sqrt{81}\). Therefore \(5\sqrt{3} < 9\).
Write both as single square roots: \(7 = \sqrt{49}\) and \(2\sqrt{5} = \sqrt{4 \times 5} = \sqrt{20}\). Since \(49 > 20\), we get \(\sqrt{49} > \sqrt{20}\). Therefore \(7 > 2\sqrt{5}\).

These are like surds, so add their coefficients: \(5\sqrt{3} + 8\sqrt{3} = (5 + 8)\sqrt{3} = 13\sqrt{3}\).

solution: First simplify \(\sqrt{125} = \sqrt{25 \times 5} = 5\sqrt{5}\). Then all three terms are like surds: \(9\sqrt{5} - 4\sqrt{5} + 5\sqrt{5} = (9 - 4 + 5)\sqrt{5} = 10\sqrt{5}\).

Simplify each surd first: \(\sqrt{48} = \sqrt{16 \times 3} = 4\sqrt{3}\) and \(\sqrt{27} = \sqrt{9 \times 3} = 3\sqrt{3}\). So the expression becomes \(7 \times 4\sqrt{3} - 3\sqrt{3} - \sqrt{3} = 28\sqrt{3} - 3\sqrt{3} - \sqrt{3} = (28 - 3 - 1)\sqrt{3} = 24\sqrt{3}\).
All three terms are like surds, so add their coefficients: \(\left(1 - \frac{3}{5} + 2\right)\sqrt{7} = \left(\frac{5 - 3 + 10}{5}\right)\sqrt{7} = \frac{12}{5}\sqrt{7}\).
\(3\sqrt{12} \times \sqrt{18} = 3\sqrt{12 \times 18} = 3\sqrt{216}\). Now \(216 = 36 \times 6\), so \(\sqrt{216} = 6\sqrt{6}\). Therefore the product is \(3 \times 6\sqrt{6} = 18\sqrt{6}\).

\(3\sqrt{12} \times 7\sqrt{15} = (3 \times 7)\sqrt{12 \times 15} = 21\sqrt{180}\). Now \(180 = 36 \times 5\), so \(\sqrt{180} = 6\sqrt{5}\). Therefore the product is \(21 \times 6\sqrt{5} = 126\sqrt{5}\).
\(3\sqrt{8} \times \sqrt{5} = 3\sqrt{8 \times 5} = 3\sqrt{40}\). Now \(40 = 4 \times 10\), so \(\sqrt{40} = 2\sqrt{10}\). Therefore the product is \(3 \times 2\sqrt{10} = 6\sqrt{10}\).
\(5\sqrt{8} \times 2\sqrt{8} = (5 \times 2)\left(\sqrt{8} \times \sqrt{8}\right) = 10 \times 8 = 80\).

\(\sqrt{125} \div \sqrt{50} = \sqrt{\frac{125}{50}} = \sqrt{\frac{5}{2}}\). Rationalizing the denominator, \(\sqrt{\frac{5}{2}} = \frac{\sqrt{5}}{\sqrt{2}} \times \frac{\sqrt{2}}{\sqrt{2}} = \frac{\sqrt{10}}{2}\).
\(\sqrt{54} \div \sqrt{27} = \sqrt{\frac{54}{27}} = \sqrt{2}\).
\(\sqrt{310} \div \sqrt{5} = \sqrt{\frac{310}{5}} = \sqrt{62}\), and 62 has no square factor, so this is the simplest form.
Multiply numerator and denominator by \(\sqrt{5}\): \(\frac{3}{\sqrt{5}} \times \frac{\sqrt{5}}{\sqrt{5}} = \frac{3\sqrt{5}}{5}\).
Multiply numerator and denominator by \(\sqrt{14}\): \(\frac{1}{\sqrt{14}} \times \frac{\sqrt{14}}{\sqrt{14}} = \frac{\sqrt{14}}{14}\).
Multiply numerator and denominator by \(\sqrt{7}\): \(\frac{5}{\sqrt{7}} \times \frac{\sqrt{7}}{\sqrt{7}} = \frac{5\sqrt{7}}{7}\).
Multiply numerator and denominator by \(\sqrt{3}\): \(\frac{6}{9\sqrt{3}} \times \frac{\sqrt{3}}{\sqrt{3}} = \frac{6\sqrt{3}}{9 \times 3} = \frac{6\sqrt{3}}{27} = \frac{2\sqrt{3}}{9}\).
Multiply numerator and denominator by \(\sqrt{3}\): \(\frac{11}{\sqrt{3}} \times \frac{\sqrt{3}}{\sqrt{3}} = \frac{11\sqrt{3}}{3}\).
